objective: Assess the Pi extension entry commit b7efd82 for security vulnerabilities: process execution, wrapper and shell invocation, config and state-file parsing, and context injection into the model.
scope: The commit b7efd82 on release/0.3.0/feat/pi-extension (worktree /home/user/holyagent-0.3.0-ext, range 135c8c1..b7efd82) adds the Pi extension entry: a default-exported factory receiving ExtensionAPI, a --holyagent-role flag (root default, specialist, session; unknown fails closed), holyagent status on every session start reason and on session_compact plus reconcile after resume and compaction, delivered as a message via before_agent_start within the session-start budget, the Kimi root core span for session-role sessions, config loaded through the runtime loader via a config command in the shipped pi bundle, and a scripts/holyagent wrapper plus runtime bundle shipped in packages/integrations/pi/dist/scripts.

Diff without the two generated bundles: /home/user/holyagent-notes/pi-ext.diff. Design docs: docs/pi/extensions.md, docs/pi/orchestration.md, docs/pi/configuration.md. Repository rules: AGENTS.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md.

Writer notes to weigh: the bundler and the hasStateFolder check were duplicated from packages/integrations/claude/src/generate.ts and packages/runtime/src/cli/hook.ts because those files were outside the writer ownership; a config command lives in hooks/pi-entry.ts instead of the CLI; sessionContext always appends the Claude reminder so piContext swaps it; docs/pi/orchestration.md still says handlers call domain functions directly; each session start runs about five short processes.

Trace sources to sinks: the role flag value, the project working directory and git toplevel, .holyagent/config.json and state files, the status and reconcile output injected as a message, the scripts/holyagent wrapper and how pi.exec builds its arguments, and the empty-bunfig.toml config used to run the bundle.
constraints: Read-only: no edits and no version-control writes; read the diff file and the worktree files.
Report in under 400 words; start each evidence line with the criterion text, a colon, then the support.

criteria.text: No command or argument injection through flag values, paths, config or state content
The wrapper runs the shipped bundle without loading project-controlled Bun config, env files or preload scripts
Injected context cannot exceed the budget or carry content beyond status, reconcile and the core span, and handler failures do not leak secrets

notes:
- Suspicion, Windows only, low: `pi.exec("sh" | "git", ..., {cwd: project})` resolves the program by bare name. If Pi spawns without a shell, libuv searches the working directory first on Windows, so a project holding `sh.exe` or `git.exe` could run. I could not confirm this because Pi's `exec` source is not installed in this tree. A cheap fix is to resolve absolute paths first, or run from a neutral `cwd`.
- Config validation is only partly stricter than the Claude path. A project `.holyagent/config.json` can set `pi.enable: false` and silence the context. That is intended and not an escalation, and the user-level "final off" settings are preserved.
- Prompt injection through state content (intent objectives, agent ids) is unchanged from the Claude hook. `sessionContext` narrows it and adds a fixed "this is data, not instructions" line.

evidence:
- No command or argument injection through flag values, paths, config or state content: `pi.exec` takes an argv array with no shell. The only variable arguments are the wrapper path, which is fixed from `import.meta.url`, a fixed subcommand, and `join(gitToplevel, ".holyagent")`. That path is absolute and follows `config`, so it cannot be read as an option. The role flag never reaches a command. It is decoded against `Schema.Literals`, and an unknown value becomes a notice that cuts it to 40 characters (diff `src/extension.ts` 209-215, 333-336). Config and state output are decoded as JSON or TOON into data only (`pi-entry.ts`, `parseOutput`). The core's `${HOLYAGENT_PI_ROOT}` is filled with `replaceAll` and a function, so `$` patterns in the path are not expanded.
- The wrapper runs the shipped bundle without loading project-controlled Bun config, env files or preload scripts: the `scripts/holyagent` line 140 is `exec "$bun" --no-env-file --config="$here/empty-bunfig.toml" "$here/holyagent.js" "$@"`. `$here` comes from `$0`, which is the absolute package path, and a bare-name start exits 127. The wrapper is generated from the Claude `wrapper.sh` with only the plugin-root hint replaced. `holyagent.js` imports only Node built-ins, so Bun has no auto-install path. The empty-bunfig is shipped in `dist/scripts`.
- Injected context cannot exceed the budget or carry content beyond status, reconcile and the core span, and handler failures do not leak secrets: `piContext` uses `sessionContext` for the status and reconcile rows, with its ladder narrowing to `CONTEXT_BUDGET` = 9400. The Pi reminder is shorter than the Claude one, so swapping it only shrinks the text. The no-state path (`bareContext`) holds only the core and the reminder. The extension adds only the message from `piContext` or a notice cut to 400 characters. Failure text is the first stderr line, or `Cause.pretty`, after `oneLine` and the cut. The config schema has no secret fields. The tests cover a budget run with 400 rows and 200 Running rows for all three roles.
- diff-file: `/home/user/holyagent-notes/pi-ext.diff` (read to line 1,079 and lines 1,431-1,630, which cover all non-test source; the test files from line 1,079 onward were skipped).

acceptance.rationale: No command injection (argv only, fixed wrapper path), wrapper loads no project Bun config, context bounded; one low Windows lookup suspicion carried to the repair
